title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ལ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 105)
shelf_note: A Madhyamaka commentary refuting Cittamatra and self-cognition (svasamvedana); it quotes the bodhicitta verse 'rtogs bya rtogs byed rnam pa'i sems' and runs a fourfold analysis of mind and illusion, so it belongs in the dbu ma section.
structure_note: The margin folio label on the image reads '416' while the record is page 415. That is probably a scan-sequence versus folio-label offset, not a defect. The page continues mid-sentence from the previous leaf, as expected.

ocr_errors.image: the last syllable of the verse line may be ཅན rather than པ (hard to read at this resolution)
ocr_errors.problem: possible one-syllable slip in the verse; no change of meaning

tr_errors_A.english: It is the ultimate truth because it is not an imputation through realization; this meaning is further emphasized.
tr_errors_A.problem: This is a word gloss (the 'yang' in the root text means 'moreover'), and A turns it into 'this meaning is further emphasized'. A also makes the ཏེ into a causal 'because'.

tr_errors_A.english: The origin of suffering is the world, and viewpoints and cravings are also just that
tr_errors_A.problem: The quoted verse is a list (suffering, origin, the world, the bases of views and craving are those very [aggregates]). A misparses it as the claim 'the origin of suffering is the world'.

tr_errors_A.english: Whatever the Blessed One has said regarding the existence of Cittamatra
tr_errors_A.problem: The source means the Buddha taught that things exist as mind only. A has him talking about the existence of the Cittamatra school.

tr_errors_A.english: even a slight knowledge of svasamvedana is not logical
tr_errors_A.problem: The source says self-cognizing awareness is not tenable at all. 'Knowledge of' is awkward and misleading.

tr_errors_A.english: the philosophical tenet that asserts the world is mind-only

tr_errors_B.english: The entry into positing the appropriated aggregates as existent, non-existent, and so forth through conceptual investigation is the very cause of saṃsāra.
tr_errors_B.problem: The source says the cause of engaging in such positing IS samsara. B makes the positing the cause OF samsara, which swaps subject and predicate.
'brel pa ma yin means 'not connected / irrelevant', not 'incoherent'

tr_errors_B.english: Not even the slightest real entity is refuted here.
tr_errors_B.problem: The word 'real' is added; it is a slight interpretive gloss

pages.prefer_reason: Neither version has a serious error, but A misparses the opening word gloss, the quoted verse and the mind-only sentence, while B has a single moderate subject-predicate swap.

book_verdict: This is a cleanly transcribed folio of a Madhyamaka commentary, on the right shelf. Both English versions are serviceable; B is the more faithful of the two.
